body:
Full-codebase review, smaller Android findings, verified by reading:

* The overview's expense cards go stale. The summary collector is driven by `listsRepo.activeLists()` alone, but recomputes from the items table; adding or editing an entry touches only items and does not move the list row, so the card keeps the old net total and balance until process death or a pull-to-refresh. `ExpenseListViewModel` already combines an items flow — do the same here.
* Pending and blocked counts are invisible exactly when they matter. `SyncStatus` is in-memory and only ever written by a sync run, and every scheduled sync requires connectivity, so after a cold start offline the marker shows no pending count and the "needs attention" banner for quarantined rows is gone. Seed it from `dirtyRows().size` / `blockedRowCount()` at start-up.
* `ExpenseListViewModel` numbers former members from `itemsForList` (excludes backlog) while `ExpenseFormViewModel` uses `activeItemsForListOnce` (includes it), so the numbering can disagree between the ledger and the form.
* `androidx.activity.ComponentActivity` is declared `exported="true"` in the MAIN source set, so it ships in release and any app can launch a blank activity in this task. It is there for release unit tests; a test-only manifest or `exported="false"` would do.
* `res/xml/file_paths.xml` roots the whole filesDir (which holds the DataStore files) rather than just the crash log. Only granted URIs are readable, so defence in depth only.
* `AppVersionResponse` omits the `protocol` field the wire contract documents as what a 426'd client reads to learn what it must catch up to; the checker infers it from the version string instead.
title: Android: smaller review findings (stale overview cards, invisible counts, manifest, numbering)
